subject: 2-species model with interaction, categorical factor and continuous covariate

messages.author: 0c69c6d399345fab
messages.subject: 2-species model with interaction, categorical factor and continuous covariate
parts:
To all,

I hope everyone is doing well, and I sincerely appreciate all of the help and advice I've
received from this forum.

With that being said, I have another error I'm running into while constructing 2-species models. The model structure allows for there to be an interaction between species A and species B (where species B is the subordinate species). I wish to know how the two parameters psiBA and psiBa change in relation to "forest". Also, I am attempting to estimate how drainage area (DA) influences the occupancy of species  A & B. Forest is a categorical factor with three levels. Right, now I am modeling psiBa as a function of forest, and using the ifelse statement to specify that I wish to calculate psiBA for each site dependent on the value of DA . I'm also attempting to calculate psiA for each level of forest. I planned on using the equations specified in Richmond et al. 2010 to estimate the parameters not included in the model (e.g., psi B). As of right now, the code is producing an error which states, "compilation error on line 5, attempt to redefine node psiA". Detection is assumed to be constant for both species, and species A does not interfere with the detection of species B. 

Any help with this would be much appreciated. Code is below, data is attached.

Thanks!

Josh

####2-Species Occupancy Models
#Creek Chub and Goldstripe Darter
install.packages("mcmcOutput")
library(mcmcOutput)

data<-read.csv("SA_GD_coexist.csv", header = T, row.names = "Site")

#Convert intergers > 0 to 1
occ<-ifelse(data[,3:10]>0,1,0)

# Separate the two detection histories
DHA <- as.matrix(occ[, 5:8])
DHB <- as.matrix(occ[, 1:4])

#Aggregate detection data
yA <- rowSums(DHA)
yB <- rowSums(DHB)

nSites <- nrow(data)
zA <- ifelse(yA > 0, 1, NA)
zB <- ifelse(yB > 0, 1, NA)

#Site Covariates
library(robustHD)
DA<- as.numeric(standardize(data$DA))
Forest<- as.integer(data$Forest)

##2-Species Model With Interaction, Site Covariate (DA), & Categorical Factor (Forest)
#data 
jagsData <- list(yA = yA, yB = yB, n = 4, nSites = nSites,
                 zA = zA, zB = zB, DA = DA, Forest=Forest, nCat=3)

require(jagsUI)
#Model
sink("mod3.txt")
cat("model{
  # Likelihood
  for(i in 1:nSites) {
     # Ecological model
     logit(psiA[i]) <- A0[Forest[i]] + aDA * DA[i]
     logit(psiBA[i]) <- B0 + bDA * DA[i] 
     zA[i] ~ dbern(psiA[i])
     zB[i] ~ dbern(ifelse(zA[i], psiBA[i], psiBa[Forest[i]]))
     # Observation model
    yA[i] ~ dbin(pA * zA[i], n)
    yB[i] ~ dbin(pB * zB[i], n)
  }

  # Priors
  # Priors
  B0 ~ dunif(-5,5)
  aDA ~ dunif(-5, 5)
  bDA ~ dunif(-5, 5)
  pA~ dbeta(1,1)
  pB~ dbeta(1,1)
  for(i in 1:nCat) {
  psiBa[i]~ dunif(0,1)
  psiA[i] ~ dunif(0,1)
  A0[i]<- logit(psiA[i])
    }
}
",fill=TRUE)
sink()

#Parameters Estimated
wanted <- c("A0","B0", "aDA", "bDA", "psiBa", "pA", "pB")

#Run Model
Int_DA<- jags(jagsData, NULL, wanted, model="mod3.txt",
              n.chains=3, n.burnin = 5000, n.adapt=1000, n.iter=10000,
              parallel=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: 2-species model with interaction, categorical factor and continuous covariate
parts:
Hi Josh,

The "attempt to redefine node" error means that you have given a variable, in this case psiA, two conflicting definitions in your JAGS code.

In this case, you have in your ecological model:

but also in your priors:
psiA[i] ~ dunif(0,1)

You can only have one of these!

As you build up the complexity of your models, especially if adapting code from one model to the next, it's always worth checking through the rest of the code to make sure you haven't introduced a contradiction.

Cheers,

Josh (a different one!)
